title: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
Every page of an app with a sidebar fails axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule (impact: critical, WCAG 2.0 A,
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value), and so does every `st.date_input`. In both cases `aria-expanded` is set on an
element whose role does not support it:

1. The sidebar is rendered as a plain `<section>` with no accessible name, so it has no landmark role that
   supports `aria-expanded`. `frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~265):
   `aria-expanded={!isCollapsed}` on the `Resizable` rendered as `StyledSidebar`.
2. The date input's field is a `<div>` with no role carrying `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
   `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DateInput/SingleDateInput.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~553); the same pattern
   is in `RangeDateInput.tsx`.

Assistive technology ignores (or mis-announces) state on an element it cannot map to a role, so the
expanded/collapsed state is not conveyed, and automated audits (axe, Lighthouse) report a critical failure
that app authors cannot fix from Python.

### Reproducible Code Example
```python
import datetime
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.write("Sidebar content")
st.date_input("Start date", datetime.date(2026, 1, 1))
st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))
```

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Run axe-core 4.13 (e.g. `[USER]/playwright` with tags `wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa`)
   against the page, at 1280px or 390px wide.

### Expected Behavior
No `aria-allowed-attr` violations.

### Current Behavior
```
aria-allowed-attr (critical, wcag2a, wcag412) — 2 nodes
<section class="stSidebar st-emotion-cache-1kss9tm e16xr0mu0" data-testid="stSidebar" aria-expanded="true" style="position: relative; ...">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="true"
<div aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowDown" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" data-testid="stDateInputField" class="st-emotion-cache-11mhraf ekyilc22">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="false"
```
(At 390px the sidebar starts collapsed and the same node reports `aria-expanded="false"`.)

### Suggested fix
- **Sidebar:** put the state on the control, not the region. Remove `aria-expanded` from the `<section>`;
  set `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls="<sidebar id>"` on the collapse/expand buttons
  (`stSidebarCollapseButton` / `stExpandSidebarButton`), which already carry `aria-label`s since #14563.
  Optionally give the section an accessible name (`aria-label="Sidebar"`) so it becomes a `region` landmark.
- **Date input:** follow the React Aria DatePicker pattern the widget is now built on: the field is
  `role="group"` (labelled by the widget label) and the popup state lives on the element that opens the
  calendar. Either move `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-keyshortcuts` to a
  calendar toggle `<button>`, or, if the whole field must stay the trigger, give it a role that supports
  them. (It contains spinbuttons, so `role="button"` would nest interactive content; a separate button is
  the clean option.)

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No — sidebar has had it for several releases; the date input form arrived with the non-BaseWeb
  DateInput (#16460, 1.62).

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI, Chromium via Playwright) and Windows 11 (Chromium)
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)
- axe-core: 4.13.0

### Additional Information
Found by a WCAG 2.2 AA gate that runs axe on every page of several Streamlit apps at 390px and 1280px;
these are the only `aria-allowed-attr` findings left in those apps and none is reachable from app code.

comments.body:
This is a valid WCAG 2.0 A (4.1.2) bug: `aria-expanded` is applied to elements whose implicit roles do not allow it, so axe `aria-allowed-attr` fails on every app with a sidebar and every `st.date_input`. The sidebar is a nameless `<section>` (`StyledSidebar`) with `aria-expanded={!isCollapsed}` in `frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx`; without an accessible name it is not a landmark, and `aria-expanded` is not allowed on a generic section. The date field is a `<div>` (`StyledDateInputWrapper`) with `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` in `SingleDateInput.tsx` and `RangeDateInput.tsx` — the same pattern is also on `st.datetime_input` (`SingleDateTimeInput.tsx`). The reporter’s fix direction matches ARIA: put expanded state on the actual controls (sidebar collapse/expand buttons; a calendar toggle or a role that supports those attributes). Note that [#14563](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14563) (intended to add `aria-label`s on those sidebar buttons) was closed stale and never merged; `BaseButton` currently defaults to `aria-label=""`. Existing unit tests assert `aria-expanded` on `stSidebar` itself and would need to be updated with the fix.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8399 — Umbrella request for basic web accessibility (landmarks, accessible names). The unmerged sidebar-button labeling PR (#14563) was filed as a partial fix for this issue; naming the sidebar region and its collapse/expand controls overlaps this work.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16607 — Related ARIA naming bug: `st.iframe` uses a hard-coded accessible name, so assistive tech cannot distinguish embeds. Same class of WCAG 4.1.2 name/role/value problem, different widget.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12873 — Section 508 / assistive-tech compliance for widget chrome (decorative graphics announced by screen readers). Not a duplicate, but the same automated-audit / compliance motivation as this axe finding.
